# Part 2b: Understanding GAM Modeling (What is GAM Detecting?)

## Investigating GAM's Statistical Model

```{r gam-modeling-analysis, message=FALSE}
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# DIAGNOSTIC 9: Understanding GAM's Parametric Assumptions
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# GAM detects STRONG interactions, but K-W (rank-based) does not.
# Possible explanations:
# 1. GAM is fitting PARAMETRIC structure (mean + variance) beyond just test of ranks
# 2. GAM is sensitive to OUTLIERS or LEVERAGE POINTS
# 3. GAM residuals are NORMALLY distributed, giving extra power (if Gaussian assumption valid)
# 4. K-W only tests if RANKS differ, misses linear/smooth trends in magnitude
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

cat("=== DIAGNOSTIC 9: WHAT IS GAM MODELING? ===\n\n")

# For each top GAM gene, examine:
# 1. Distribution of residuals (are they normal?)
# 2. Fitted pattern across Q-levels
# 3. Leverage/influence points (outliers driving GAM signal)
# 4. Heteroscedasticity (does variance change with Q?)

top_gam_genes <- head(comparison$gene[order(comparison$p_interaction)], 5)

cat("Detailed Analysis of Top 5 GAM-Significant Genes:\n\n")

gam_diagnostics <- list()

for (g_idx in seq_along(top_gam_genes)) {
  gene_name <- top_gam_genes[g_idx]
  gam_pval <- comparison$p_interaction[comparison$gene == gene_name]
  gam_family <- comparison$family_used[comparison$gene == gene_name]
  gam_hetero <- comparison$heteroscedasticity_detected[comparison$gene == gene_name]
  
  cat(sprintf("─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n"))
  cat(sprintf("Gene %d: %s\n", g_idx, gene_name))
  cat(sprintf("  GAM p-value: %.2e\n", gam_pval))
  cat(sprintf("  Family used: %s\n", gam_family))
  cat(sprintf("  Heteroscedasticity detected: %s\n", gam_hetero))
  
  # Get gene data
  gene_idx <- which(test_genes == gene_name)
  if (length(gene_idx) > 0) {
    gene_entropy <- entropy_matrix[gene_idx, ]
    gene_coldata <- data.frame(
      entropy = as.numeric(gene_entropy),
      q = ts_coldata$q,
      sample_type = ts_coldata$sample_type
    )
    
    # Check for outliers using IQR method
    q1 <- quantile(gene_coldata$entropy, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE)
    q3 <- quantile(gene_coldata$entropy, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)
    iqr <- q3 - q1
    lower_bound <- q1 - 1.5 * iqr
    upper_bound <- q3 + 1.5 * iqr
    
    n_outliers <- sum(gene_coldata$entropy < lower_bound | gene_coldata$entropy > upper_bound, na.rm = TRUE)
    pct_outliers <- 100 * n_outliers / sum(!is.na(gene_coldata$entropy))
    
    cat(sprintf("  Outliers (IQR method): %d (%.1f%%)\n", n_outliers, pct_outliers))
    
    # Fit linear model to get residuals and assess normality
    lm_fit <- try(lm(entropy ~ factor(q), data = gene_coldata), silent = TRUE)
    
    if (!inherits(lm_fit, "try-error")) {
      residuals <- residuals(lm_fit)
      fitted_vals <- fitted(lm_fit)
      
      # Shapiro-Wilk test for normality
      sw_test <- try(shapiro.test(residuals), silent = TRUE)
      if (!inherits(sw_test, "try-error")) {
        cat(sprintf("  Residual normality (Shapiro-Wilk): p=%.4f\n", sw_test$p.value))
        if (sw_test$p.value < 0.05) {
          cat(sprintf("    ⚠ Residuals are NON-NORMAL (may violate GAM Gaussian assumption)\n"))
        } else {
          cat(sprintf("    ✓ Residuals appear normal\n"))
        }
      }
      
      # Variance by Q-level
      cat("  Entropy by Q-level:\n")
      for (q_val in sort(unique(as.numeric(gene_coldata$q)))) {
        q_entropy <- gene_coldata$entropy[as.numeric(gene_coldata$q) == q_val]
        q_var <- var(q_entropy, na.rm = TRUE)
        q_mean <- mean(q_entropy, na.rm = TRUE)
        q_n <- sum(!is.na(q_entropy))
        
        cat(sprintf("    Q=%.1f: n=%d, mean=%.4f, var=%.4f, sd=%.4f\n",
                    q_val, q_n, q_mean, q_var, sqrt(q_var)))
      }
      
      # Store for comparison
      gam_diagnostics[[gene_name]] <- list(
        n_outliers = n_outliers,
        pct_outliers = pct_outliers,
        normality_pvalue = if(!inherits(sw_test, "try-error")) sw_test$p.value else NA,
        residuals = residuals,
        fitted = fitted_vals
      )
    }
  }
  
  cat("\n")
}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# DIAGNOSTIC 10: GAM vs K-W Comparison - Why the Disagreement?
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

cat("\n\n=== DIAGNOSTIC 10: WHY GAM AND K-W DISAGREE ===\n\n")

cat("Hypothesis Testing Comparison:\n\n")

cat("Kruskal-Wallis (K-W - Rank-Based):\n")
cat("  H0: The distribution of ranks is the SAME across Q-levels\n")
cat("  Ha: The distribution of ranks DIFFERS across Q-levels\n")
cat("  Sensitive to: Changes in CENTER (median)\n")
cat("  NOT sensitive to: Changes in SPREAD (variance)\n")
cat("  Assumption: Shapes of distributions are similar across groups\n")
cat("  Power: Robust to non-normality, good general-purpose test\n\n")

cat("GAM (Parametric - Generalized Additive Model):\n")
cat("  H0: The LINEAR+SMOOTH MEAN entropy is the SAME across Q-levels\n")
cat("  Ha: The LINEAR+SMOOTH MEAN entropy DIFFERS across Q-levels\n")
cat("  Sensitive to: Changes in MEAN and VARIANCE structure\n")
cat("  NOT sensitive to: Distribution shape (fitted to expected distribution)\n")
cat("  Assumption: Gaussian/Gamma family structure appropriate for data\n")
cat("  Power: High power if assumptions met; violates assumptions → spurious signal\n\n")

cat("Key Insight: GAM and K-W test DIFFERENT hypotheses!\n")
cat("  - If GAM assumption (Gaussian mean structure) is WRONG → False positives\n")
cat("  - If K-W assumption (similar shapes) is WRONG → False negatives\n\n")

# Check if GAM residuals are actually normal
if (length(gam_diagnostics) > 0) {
  gam_normality_results <- sapply(gam_diagnostics, function(x) {
    !is.na(x$normality_pvalue) && x$normality_pvalue < 0.05
  })
  gam_normality_violations <- sum(as.numeric(gam_normality_results), na.rm = TRUE)
  
  if (gam_normality_violations > 0) {
    cat(sprintf("⚠ WARNING: %d of %d top GAM genes have NON-NORMAL residuals\n",
                gam_normality_violations, length(gam_diagnostics)))
    cat("  This suggests GAM's Gaussian assumption may be violated\n")
    cat("  Result: GAM may be detecting false positives from model misspecification\n\n")
  } else {
    cat(sprintf("✓ All %d top GAM genes have NORMALLY distributed residuals\n", length(gam_diagnostics)))
    cat("  This supports GAM's Gaussian assumption\n\n")
  }
} else {
  cat("⚠ No genes analyzed in GAM diagnostics\n")
}

# Check for high outlier percentages
if (length(gam_diagnostics) > 0) {
  high_outlier_genes <- Filter(function(x) x$pct_outliers > 10, gam_diagnostics)
  if (length(high_outlier_genes) > 0) {
    cat(sprintf("⚠ WARNING: %d of %d top GAM genes have >10%% outliers\n",
                length(high_outlier_genes), length(gam_diagnostics)))
    cat("  Outliers can drive parametric/semi-parametric tests (GEE) but not rank tests (K-W)\n")
    cat("  Result: Disagreement may be due to leverage points\n\n")
  }
}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# RECOMMENDATION
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

cat("\n=== INTERPRETATION & RECOMMENDATION ===\n\n")

cat("If GAM's Gaussian assumption is valid AND residuals are normal:\n")
cat("  ✓ GAM has higher statistical power\n")
cat("  ✓ GAM results preferred (with K-W as supporting validation)\n")
cat("  ⚠ K-W's inability to detect effects may be its limitation, not GAM's fault\n\n")

cat("If GAM's assumptions are violated (non-normal residuals, outliers):\n")
cat("  ⚠ GAM may have spurious positives\n")
cat("  ✓ Trust K-W results more (K-W is robust to assumption violations)\n")
cat("  → Report both methods but emphasize K-W for agreement\n\n")

cat("Next Step: Check boundary clustering fix (now disabled for entropy)\n")
cat("  Re-run with updated rank_test_improvements.R\n")
cat("  K-W should now detect meaningful Q-effects if they exist\n")
```

# Part 7: Diagnostic Visualization for Method Disagreement

## Understanding Disagreement Patterns

When methods disagree, it's NOT a bug—it reflects different perspectives on the same data:

| Scenario | GEE Detects | Rank-Based Detects | Interpretation | Action |
|----------|------------|-------------------|---|---|
| **Both significant** | Smooth trend in mean | Median/distribution shift | Very robust signal | ✅ Report with high confidence |
| **Only GEE significant** | Smooth/linear trend | — | Smooth trend, possibly heteroscedastic | ⚠ Check variance pattern; note method selection |
| **Only rank-based significant** | — | Median/step-wise change or robust shift | Non-linear or distribution change | ⚠ Inspect for step-wise patterns |
| **Neither significant** | — | — | No clear q-interaction | ✓ Not significant |

## Diagnostic Code: Categorizing Genes by Agreement

```{r diagnostic-categorize-genes, eval=FALSE}
# Assuming you have:
# - lm_res: GEE results with p_interaction
# - kw_res: Rank-based results with p_value (or adj_p_value from multicorr)
# - Both with same gene names

# Set significance threshold
alpha <- 0.05

# Merge results
merged <- cbind(
  gene = rownames(lm_res),
  gee_p = lm_res$p_interaction,
  rank_p = kw_res$p_value
)

# Create categories
merged$category <- NA
merged$category[merged$gee_p < alpha & merged$rank_p < alpha] <- "Both Sig"
merged$category[merged$gee_p < alpha & merged$rank_p >= alpha] <- "GEE Only"
merged$category[merged$gee_p >= alpha & merged$rank_p < alpha] <- "Rank-Based Only"
merged$category[merged$gee_p >= alpha & merged$rank_p >= alpha] <- "Neither"

# Summary
cat("Method Agreement Summary:\n")
cat("Both significant:       ", sum(merged$category == "Both Sig"), "genes\n")
cat("GEE only:               ", sum(merged$category == "GEE Only"), "genes\n")
cat("Rank-based only:        ", sum(merged$category == "Rank-Based Only"), "genes\n")
cat("Neither significant:    ", sum(merged$category == "Neither"), "genes\n\n")

# Correlation
correlation <- cor(merged$gee_p, merged$rank_p, method = "spearman")
cat("Spearman correlation (GEE vs Rank-based p-values):", sprintf("%.3f", correlation), "\n\n")
```

## Diagnostic Code: Visualizing Disagreement

```{r diagnostic-visualize-agreement, eval=FALSE, fig.width=14, fig.height=6}
library(ggplot2)
library(gridExtra)

# Define significance threshold
alpha <- 0.05
sig_threshold <- -log10(alpha)

# 1. SCATTER PLOT: GEE vs Rank-based p-values with concordance quadrants
p1 <- ggplot(merged, aes(x = -log10(gee_p), y = -log10(rank_p), color = category)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, size = 3) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = sig_threshold, linetype = "dashed", color = "red", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = sig_threshold, linetype = "dashed", color = "red", linewidth = 0.8) +
  # Add quadrant labels
  annotate("text", x = 0.5, y = Inf, label = "GEE Only", vjust = 1.5, hjust = 0, color = "blue", size = 4) +
  annotate("text", x = Inf, y = 0.5, label = "Rank Only", vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1, color = "orange", size = 4) +
  annotate("text", x = Inf, y = Inf, label = "Both Sig", vjust = 1, hjust = 1, color = "darkgreen", size = 4) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("Both Sig" = "darkgreen", "GEE Only" = "blue", 
               "Rank-Based Only" = "orange", "Neither" = "gray"),
    limits = c("Both Sig", "GEE Only", "Rank-Based Only", "Neither"),
    na.value = "gray"
  ) +
  xlab("-log10(GEE p-value)") +
  ylab("-log10(Rank-based p-value)") +
  ggtitle("Method Concordance: GEE vs Rank-Based Q-Interaction Tests") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "topright",
    plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 10)
  )

# 2. BAR PLOT: Gene counts by category (only categories present in data)
cat_counts <- as.data.frame(table(merged$category))
colnames(cat_counts) <- c("Category", "Count")
# Ensure proper ordering
cat_counts$Category <- factor(cat_counts$Category, 
                              levels = c("Both Sig", "GEE Only", "Rank-Based Only", "Neither"))
cat_counts <- cat_counts[order(cat_counts$Category), ]

color_map <- c("Both Sig" = "darkgreen", "GEE Only" = "blue", 
               "Rank-Based Only" = "orange", "Neither" = "gray")
colors_used <- color_map[as.character(cat_counts$Category)]

p2 <- ggplot(cat_counts, aes(x = Category, y = Count, fill = Category)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(aes(label = Count), vjust = -0.5, size = 4, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = color_map,
    limits = c("Both Sig", "GEE Only", "Rank-Based Only", "Neither"),
    na.value = "gray"
  ) +
  xlab("Agreement Category") +
  ylab("Number of Genes") +
  ggtitle("Gene Distribution by Method Agreement") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 10),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10)
  )

# Combine and display
combined_plot <- grid.arrange(p1, p2, ncol = 2, widths = c(1, 0.8))
print(combined_plot)

# Print summary statistics
cat("\n=== METHOD CONCORDANCE SUMMARY ===\n")
cat("Spearman correlation (GEE vs Rank p-values):", 
    sprintf("%.3f\n", cor(merged$gee_p, merged$rank_p, method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs")))
cat("\nGene Counts by Category:\n")
print(cat_counts)
```

## Diagnostic Code: Inspecting Problematic Genes

```{r diagnostic-inspect-discordant, eval=FALSE}
# Ensure merged has gene names in accessible format
if (!("gene" %in% colnames(merged))) {
  merged <- cbind(gene = rownames(merged), merged)
}

# Find genes with largest disagreement (high p-value difference)
merged$p_diff <- abs(merged$gee_p - merged$rank_p)
discordant <- merged[order(-merged$p_diff), ][1:10, ]

cat("\n=== Top 10 Most Discordant Genes ===\n")
cat("(Sorted by largest absolute p-value difference between GEE and Rank-based)\n\n")
print_cols <- intersect(c("gene", "gee_p", "rank_p", "category", "p_diff"), colnames(discordant))
print(discordant[, print_cols])

# For each discordant gene, generate diagnostic report
cat("\n\n=== DETAILED DIAGNOSTIC REPORT ===\n")

genes_to_inspect <- discordant$gene[1:min(3, nrow(discordant))]

for (gene in genes_to_inspect) {
  cat("\n")
  cat(strrep("═", 60), "\n")
  cat("GENE: ", gene, "\n")
  cat(strrep("═", 60), "\n\n")
  
  # Basic statistics
  gee_p <- as.numeric(merged[merged$gene == gene, "gee_p"])
  rank_p <- as.numeric(merged[merged$gene == gene, "rank_p"])
  cat(sprintf("GEE p-value:        %12.3e\n", gee_p))
  cat(sprintf("Rank-based p-value: %12.3e\n", rank_p))
  cat(sprintf("Absolute difference:%12.3e\n", abs(gee_p - rank_p)))
  cat(sprintf("Category:           %s\n\n", merged[merged$gene == gene, "category"]))
  
  # Extract gene data if available
  if (exists("entropy_long") && gene %in% unique(entropy_long$gene)) {
    gene_data <- entropy_long[entropy_long$gene == gene, ]
    
    cat("─── ENTROPY DISTRIBUTION ANALYSIS ───\n")
    
    # Variance analysis by q-value
    q_unique <- sort(unique(gene_data$q))
    cat(sprintf("Q-values analyzed: %s\n\n", paste(sprintf("%.2f", q_unique), collapse = ", ")))
    
    vars <- tapply(gene_data$entropy, gene_data$q, var, na.rm = TRUE)
    means <- tapply(gene_data$entropy, gene_data$q, mean, na.rm = TRUE)
    
    cat("Variance by Q:\n")
    for (i in seq_along(vars)) {
      cat(sprintf("  Q = %.2f: σ² = %.4f, μ = %.4f\n", 
                  as.numeric(names(vars)[i]), vars[i], means[i]))
    }
    
    # Overall variance pattern
    var_ratio <- max(vars, na.rm = TRUE) / min(vars, na.rm = TRUE)
    cat(sprintf("\nVariance ratio (max/min): %.2f\n", var_ratio))
    
    if (var_ratio > 2) {
      cat("STATUS: ⚠ HETEROSCEDASTIC\n")
      cat("INTERPRETATION: Variance increases significantly across Q-values.\n")
      cat("APPROPRIATE TESTS: ART (Aligned Rank Transform), Quantile tests\n")
      cat("RECOMMENDATION: If only rank-based method significant, heteroscedasticity likely\n")
      cat("                explains GEE lack of signal (assumes homoscedasticity).\n")
    } else {
      cat("STATUS: ✓ HOMOSCEDASTIC\n")
      cat("INTERPRETATION: Variance is relatively stable across Q-values.\n")
      cat("APPROPRIATE TESTS: Standard Kruskal-Wallis or linear methods\n")
    }
    
    cat("\n─── TREND ANALYSIS ───\n")
    
    # Check monotonicity
    mean_diffs <- diff(means)
    all_pos <- all(mean_diffs > 0, na.rm = TRUE)
    all_neg <- all(mean_diffs < 0, na.rm = TRUE)
    
    if (all_pos || all_neg) {
      direction <- if (all_pos) "INCREASING" else "DECREASING"
      cat(sprintf("STATUS: ✓ MONOTONIC %s TREND\n", direction))
      cat("INTERPRETATION: Entropy changes consistently across Q-values.\n")
      cat("APPROPRIATE TESTS: GEE, linear models with smooth assumptions\n")
      cat("LIKELY REASON FOR GEE DETECTION: Consistent trend detectable by linear methods\n")
    } else {
      cat("STATUS: ⚠ NON-MONOTONIC PATTERN\n")
      cat("INTERPRETATION: Entropy changes direction or shows step-like behavior.\n")
      cat("APPROPRIATE TESTS: Rank-based, median tests, quantile tests\n")
      cat("LIKELY REASON FOR RANK-BASED DETECTION: Step-wise or median shifts\n")
    }
    
    # Visualize pattern
    cat("\nEntropy by Q: ")
    cat(sprintf("%.3f ", means))
    cat("\n")
    
    cat("\n─── BOUNDARY CLUSTERING ANALYSIS ───\n")
    
    # Check boundaries (entropy bounded by [0, log(m)])
    min_ent <- min(gene_data$entropy, na.rm = TRUE)
    max_ent <- max(gene_data$entropy, na.rm = TRUE)
    range_ent <- max_ent - min_ent
    
    cat(sprintf("Min entropy: %.4f, Max entropy: %.4f, Range: %.4f\n", 
                min_ent, max_ent, range_ent))
    
    near_lower <- min_ent / (range_ent + min_ent) < 0.1
    near_upper <- (1 - max_ent / (range_ent + max_ent)) < 0.1
    
    if (near_lower || near_upper) {
      cat("STATUS: ⚠ BOUNDARY CLUSTERING DETECTED\n")
      cat(sprintf("Close to %s boundary\n", if (near_lower) "LOWER (0)" else "UPPER"))
      cat("INTERPRETATION: Entropy constrained by [0, log(m)] bounds.\n")
      cat("APPROPRIATE TESTS: Quantile tests, non-parametric rank-based tests\n")
      cat("RECOMMENDATION: Rank-based method more suitable for boundary-affected data\n")
    } else {
      cat("STATUS: ✓ INTERIOR VALUES\n")
      cat("INTERPRETATION: Entropy well away from boundaries.\n")
      cat("APPROPRIATE TESTS: Standard parametric or non-parametric methods\n")
    }
    
  } else {
    cat("NOTE: entropy_long data not available for detailed diagnostics.\n")
    cat("Run full TSENAT.Rmd workflow to access entropy distribution analysis.\n")
  }
  
  cat("\n")
}

cat("\n" %+% strrep("═", 60) %+% "\n")
cat("INTERPRETATION SUMMARY\n")
cat(strrep("═", 60), "\n\n")
cat("For each discordant gene:\n")
cat("- HETEROSCEDASTIC pattern → Rank-based methods more appropriate\n")
cat("- MONOTONIC trend → GEE more appropriate\n")
cat("- BOUNDARY clustering → Rank-based methods more appropriate\n")
cat("- BOTH patterns present → Method selection depends on biological question\n\n")
```

## Recommendations Based on Disagreement Pattern

### If "GEE Only" genes dominate:
→ Your data has **smooth trends** in entropy  
→ GEE (with K-C correction) is appropriate primary method  
→ Rank-based methods serve as robustness checks  
→ **Report**: "GEE detected X significant q-interactions; rank-based validation identified Y

, indicating robust signals at Z genes"

### If "Rank-Based Only" genes dominate:
→ Your data has **step-wise/median shifts** or heteroscedasticity  
→ Rank-based methods catching real signal GEE misses  
→ Consider checking GEE model fit (is linear trend assumption realistic?)  
→ **Report**: "Rank-based q-interaction testing revealed X genes with significant median shifts; GEE detected Y subsets"

### If "Both Sig" genes are largest group:
→ **EXCELLENT**: Both methods agree on robust findings  
→ These genes have **strong, consistent signals**  
→ High publication confidence  
→ **Report**: "Both parametric (GEE) and non-parametric (rank-based) methods converged on X robust q-interaction genes"

---



## Publication Strategy (Both Methods with Improvements)

### When Methods Strongly Agree (r > 0.85)

✓ **Confidence Level**: VERY HIGH  
✓ **Recommendation**: Results ready for publication  
✓ **Presentation**:
  - Report both methods in main text (both now with improvements)
  - Highlight robust genes (significant in both)
  - Include test method breakdown in supplementary table
  - Note: "Both parametric and rank-based methods used adaptive improvements based on data characteristics"

### When Methods Show Moderate Agreement (r = 0.70−0.85)

✓ **Confidence Level**: MODERATE TO HIGH  
✓ **Recommendation**: Good support; compare test methods applied  
✓ **Presentation**:
  - Lead with parametric results (main analysis)
  - Report rank-based as complementary validation
  - Compare method selection (GEE fit_method) with test method selection (rank-based)
  - If heteroscedasticity detected by both → high confidence
  - Focus publication on robust gene list

### When Methods Disagree (r < 0.70)

⚠ **Confidence Level**: VARIABLE  
⚠ **Recommendation**: Investigate test method selection  
⚠ **Diagnostic checks**:
  - Which test methods were selected by each approach?
  - Are different families/tests applied to discordant genes?
  - Check if heteroscedasticity detection differs between methods
  - Review boundary clustering and skewness characteristics
  - Are genes flagged as "challenging" by improved approaches?

## Best Practices (Both Methods with Improvements - March 2026)

```{r best-practice, eval=FALSE}
# Recommended workflow with improved methods:

# 1. Run semi-parametric method with K-C correction (primary analysis)
lm_res <- calculate_lm_interaction(ts_se, method = "gee", paired = TRUE, bias_correction = TRUE)
# Returns: p_interaction (K-C corrected for small clusters), fit_method, n_clusters
# Note: K-C correction automatically applied when n_clusters < 20

# 2. Run improved rank-based validation (with conditional test selection and Hochberg correction)  
kw_res <- detect_q_gene_interactions(entropy_long, method = "kruskal.test", multicorr = "hochberg")
# Returns: p_value (raw p-value), adj_p_value (Hochberg-corrected for AR(1) q-value dependence),
#          test_method (kruskal.test/art_kw/quantile_test/robust_median_test),
#          heteroscedastic, boundary_clustered, highly_skewed for each gene

# 3. Calculate concordance accounting for method selection
correlation <- cor(lm_res$p_interaction, kw_res$p_value, method = "spearman")

# 4. Compare test selections:
#    Did GEE auto-select AR(1) correlation structure?
#    Do both methods detect heteroscedasticity for same genes?
#    Were K-C adjustments applied (n_clusters < 20)?

# 5. If high agreement:
#    Report robust genes (significant in both methods)
#    Include comparison table with correlation structures and test methods used
#    Emphasize: "Results validated with semi-parametric and rank-based methods"

# 6. If moderate agreement:
#    Analyze genes where different correlation structures were selected
#    If both selected AR(1)/ART for same gene → high confidence
#    If one selected independence and other AR(1) → investigate

# 7. If low agreement:
#    Check data quality and outliers
#    Compare heteroscedasticity detection patterns
#    Review K-C correction thresholds (n_clusters parameter)
```
